subject: Post-call: Reserved GPU onboarding & ops path (isolation + scaling)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@heliosai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: reserved GPU onboarding & ops path (isolation + scaling)

Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the suggested next steps so we have alignment before we circulate a formal MOP. TL;DR: HeliosAI is a great fit for a reserved pool with tenant isolation and burst capacity + predictable SLA for inference-heavy genAI pipelines.

Key pain points you called out:
- Model latency variability when multiple teams hit the shared endpoint (esp. morning batch peaks).
- Data isolation/compliance: you need tenant-level separation and per-tenant audit logs for PHI buffers.
- Cost predictability: current infra variability creates monthly spend noise and long provisioning lead times.

Goals we scoped on the call:
1) Provide a reserved GPU pool sized for 200 concurrent small-chat workers + 5 large-batch jobs (90% of peak QPS), with a documented warm-start profile to keep 95th-ile P99 latency under 450ms for chat paths.
2) Tenant isolation via separated runtime slices (no tenant cross-talk) + KMS-backed encryption for KV/trace artifacts.
3) A fallback policy to spin to lower-cost quantized variants if burst concurrency > committed capacity for >120s.

Operational constraints we noted:
- Helios expects a weekly deploy cadence for new model versions; KV cache invalidation must be coordinated.
- Security review requires SOC-2 evidence and a short audit of our per-request logging schema.
- Procurement prefers a quarterly invoicing cadence tied to a committed monthly GPU-hour threshold.

Proposed immediate next steps (owners):
- Diego: send draft MOP + proposed SLA matrix (attached) for an initial legal/infosec read — by EOD Wednesday.
- Ben: validate sizing assumptions and add recommended warm pool and pre-warming policy into the MOP — by Tuesday COB.
- Marissa: draft commercial term options (3/6/12m commit tiers with burst credits) and a sample invoice cadence — by Friday.
- Jordan/Priya (Helios): confirm internal teams that will need isolated endpoints (names + expected qps) and any procurement templates you require — by next Wed.

Attachments: redwood_mop_draft.pdf (working MOP outline), sla_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLA targets & metrics).

Thanks — I’ll loop legal once you confirm the list of internal Helios owners.

– Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Diego.Fernandez@redwood.com

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@heliosai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@heliosai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved GPU onboarding & ops path (isolation + scaling)

Diego — really helpful summary, thanks. Quick clarifications and a couple of datapoints from our side: we spoke to infra and product after the call and here’s what we can confirm.

Confirmed items from HeliosAI:
- Teams that need isolated endpoints: Realtime Assist (expected steady qps 120–160), Batch Gen (peaks up to ~6 large jobs concurrently), and Analytics (small qps, high embedding rate). We’ll provide a spreadsheet with team names and hourly profiles.
- Compliance: we need per-tenant audit logs retained for 12 months and access to request-level traces for incident investigations. KMS integration is required for customer-keyed encryption.
- Budget: procurement is comfortable with a committed quarterly spend that maps to ~40 A100-equivalent GPU hours/day for initial 3 months, then we’ll revisit.

Open questions for Redwood:
1) Can the reserved pool be configured with soft preemption (i.e., low-priority burst capacity that scales down gracefully without dropping active sessions)?
2) How do you recommend we handle model version toggles for canary deploys without invalidating warm caches across tenants?

We’ll send the team-level qps spreadsheet by Tuesday morning.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, HeliosAI
jordan.lee@heliosai.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved GPU onboarding & ops path (isolation + scaling)

Nice note. A couple of quick ops notes from my side:
- Sizing: 40 A100-hr/day sounds reasonable as a starting commit. I’d recommend we size the reserved registry so that warm pool holds ~20% headroom above steady-state chat workers — that gives us buffer for the 95th-ile target without burning burst credits immediately.
- Preemption: we support soft preemption via low-priority burst capacity that is best-effort; important to set a graceful fallback window (I suggest 90–150s) to avoid dropped in-progress requests.
- Cache strategy: to avoid cold starts during canaries, we can keep a small dedicated warm shard per tenant for the canary cohort and route 5% of traffic there before promoting. That avoids global cache invalidation.

I’ll tag these into the MOP doc and push an updated sla_matrix_v1.xlsx with revised numbers.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: reserved GPU onboarding & ops path (isolation + scaling)

Jordan/Priya — great, thanks for the quick confirmations. Per Ben’s notes we’ll: (1) size an initial reserved pool aligned to the 40 A100-hr/day commit, (2) propose a warm-shard strategy for canaries (5% routing) and (3) include a soft-preempt burst policy with a 120s fallback window and automatic routing to quantized variants after 2 minutes of sustained overcommit.

Attached is the working MOP and SLA matrix. Please review the following sections especially: 
- Section 2.3: Warm-pool sizing and pre-warm triggers
- Section 3.1: Tenant isolation model + audit log schema (retention: 12 months)
- Section 4.2: Burst policy and auto-fallback rules

Requested items from Helios (action items repeated):
- Team-level QPS spreadsheet (due Tue morning)
- Procurement template or PO workflow (if you have one)
- Any additional compliance evidence slice you need for SOC-2 review (we’ll pull the required artifacts)

If everything looks good, I’ll route this to Legal and Solutions for a light SOW draft next week and propose a pilot start date of 2027-04-12.

Best —
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
